clue.text: Simplest to recast with characters in unexpected places

indicators.note: to recast something is to mould it again into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An editor reworks the simplest version of a text, ending up with letters jumbled about.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: 'characters' are letters, and a word with its letters in the wrong places is MISSPELT.
explanation.definitionFit: A misspelt word has its letters wrongly ordered or chosen, so its written symbols sit where a reader would not expect them.

clue.text: Aimlessly moving, cleaning floor half-heartedly

indicators.note: doing something without heart here means losing part of the heart, the central letters, of a word

blocks.note: you clean a floor by mopping it

explanation.surface: Someone drifts around listlessly while making a feeble effort at mopping the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: MOPPING has a doubled P at its heart; losing one of them, half of that heart, leaves MOPING.
explanation.definitionFit: To mope is to wander about in a listless, dejected way, lacking any purpose or energy.

clue.text: Climbs up a sign

blocks.note: first meaning: to climb a wall or cliff hand over hand
second meaning: Libra, the zodiac sign pictured as a balance

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like someone climbing a signpost; 'a sign' is a zodiac sign, and the Scales are Libra's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means ascends by climbing, and the noun names the zodiac sign Libra, pictured as a balance.

clue.text: Kept quiet, uncommunicative

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical instruction for quiet
a reserved person keeps their thoughts to themselves

explanation.surface: Someone kept silent and gave nothing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept quiet' looks like one phrase; split it, and 'Kept' is the definition while 'quiet' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or buildings that are preserved have been maintained and protected, which is what being kept means here.

clue.text: Spooner's finding canal workers ridiculous types

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words

blocks.note: canal workers are people STAFFING LOCKS; swap the opening sounds ST and L

explanation.surface: Reverend Spooner regards the people working the canal as a comical bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Lock-keepers are STAFFING LOCKS; swapping the first sounds gives 'laffing stocks', which is how LAUGHING STOCKS is said.
explanation.definitionFit: A laughing stock is a person everyone mocks, so the plural describes people regarded as absurd objects of ridicule.

clue.text: Go silent, caught by large wildcat in retreat

indicators.note: a retreating army goes back the way it came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the puma is a big wild cat of the Americas

explanation.surface: A hunter falls quiet after being caught by a huge big cat as it backs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught by' reads as capture, but here it simply places C next to the following letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To clam up is an idiom for refusing to talk, shutting like a clam's shell.

clue.text: Liquid you make promoting health, primarily?

definitions.text: Liquid you make promoting health, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A question about some bodily fluid your body produces that keeps you well.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: its first letters spell the answer, and read straight it describes the fluid, which carries infection-fighting white cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Lymph is a clear bodily fluid the body produces, carrying white blood cells that fight infection and so help keep us healthy.

clue.text: Musical instrument that may be kept by a stoner

definitions.text: Musical instrument that may be kept by a stoner

blocks.clueFragment: Musical instrument that may be kept by a stoner
blocks.note: surface reading: a stringed instrument owned by a pot-smoking musician
setter's reading: the same word names a kitchen slicer, which sits in the drawer beside a cherry stoner

explanation.surface: A stoned musician keeps a stringed instrument lying around.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'stoner' is also a kitchen gadget that removes cherry stones; the instrument's name, also spelt with a final E, is a vegetable slicer kept in the same drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small lute-like instrument with paired metal strings, and its name also belongs to a bladed kitchen slicing tool.

clue.text: Halfwit not having arisen: it's a simple form of life

indicators.note: in a down clue, something that has risen reads from the bottom upwards, backwards

blocks.note: a plank is British slang for a stupid person, as thick as a plank
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dimwit who hasn't got out of bed is compared to a primitive organism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not having arisen' sounds like still in bed, but 'arisen' just turns the little word upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny drifting organisms in the sea, many single-celled, among the most basic living things.

clue.text: Can't fix formats misapplied in children's book

indicators.note: something misapplied is put to the wrong use, so these letters are placed wrongly and must be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A frustrated editor can't correct the formatting errors in a picture book.
explanation.walkthrough: The X and F in the fodder are the tell: few titles use both, and Roald Dahl's fox story does.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic Mr Fox is Roald Dahl's 1970 novel for young readers about a clever fox outwitting three farmers.

clue.text: Table's gold dish seen first

indicators.note: being seen first means standing at the front, so this item comes before the other

blocks.note: a plate is a dish
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A dinner table where the golden dish is the first thing guests notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' looks like furniture, but it means tableland: flat, raised ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an area of high, level ground, also called a tableland or table in geography.

clue.text: State to equip keen vicar at regular intervals

indicators.note: stepping at even spacing picks every other letter and skips the rest

blocks.note: to arm someone is to equip them with weapons
the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A country sets out to provide an enthusiastic clergyman with what he needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of 'keen vicar', not the odd ones: kEeNvIcAr.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a sovereign country in the South Caucasus, and a country is a state.

clue.text: Family member in French city, outspoken

indicators.note: outspoken means spoken out, so the word is heard rather than read

blocks.note: Nice, the Riviera city, said aloud

explanation.surface: A relative living on the Riviera is known for speaking her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken' seems to describe the relative, but it signals that the city's name is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister, so she is a relative.

clue.text: Film director, jerk, one strutting about

blocks.note: a hitch is a sudden jerk or tug
a cockerel struts around the farmyard

explanation.surface: A film-maker is dismissed as an idiot who swaggers around the set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult; it is the verb or noun for a sudden pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Hitchcock was the British-born director of Psycho, Vertigo and Rear Window, known as the master of suspense.

clue.text: Soil – mud, even – shaped for sculpture

indicators.note: shaped means moulded into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sculptor works with earth, even plain mud, moulding it into a statue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about clay modelling, which is apt, though the famous statue is marble.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venus de Milo is the celebrated armless ancient Greek marble statue displayed in the Louvre in Paris.

clue.text: Needed a kind of oil

definitions.note: an adjective describing a kind of oil, as in essential oil

blocks.note: first meaning: absolutely necessary
second meaning: the word that describes aromatic plant oils

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a request for oil; instead the two parts are separate senses of one adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means indispensable, and it also names the concentrated aromatic plant extracts called essential oils.

clue.text: Fish in mostly beer with leafy green

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: Pils is short for Pilsner, a pale lager
chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A recipe for fish cooked largely in beer and served with greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as cooking in beer, but here it only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard is a small oily sea fish of the herring family, the adult sardine.

clue.text: Everyman's assigned a counterpart that's faulty

blocks.note: the setter speaking of himself: Everyman is = I'm
to be paired is to be matched with a partner

explanation.surface: The setter complains that he has been given a defective partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for 'I', so 'Everyman's' means 'I am', shortened to I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impaired is damaged or weakened so it no longer works properly, which is being defective.

clue.text: Sometimes I cavort around Penny in shameless displays

indicators.note: to cavort is to leap and prance about wildly, so the letters jump into a new order
going around something means encircling it, so one part surrounds another

blocks.note: taken as written
d was the symbol for an old British penny, from Latin denarius

explanation.surface: The speaker admits to prancing around a woman called Penny in a brazen way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name; it is the old penny, d. The shuffled letters wrap around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodesty is indecent or brazen behaviour, so the plural means acts of flaunting oneself without shame.

clue.text: Ian and Pat involved in something that needs beating

indicators.note: involved means tangled and complicated, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two friends are caught up in some challenge they have to overcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs beating' suggests a rival to defeat; it is meant literally, a thing to be whacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinata is a decorated container full of sweets that blindfolded party guests hit with a stick until it breaks.

clue.text: Modern part of leisure centre

indicators.note: part of means a portion taken from inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A newly built section of a sports complex.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the join: leisuRE CENTre.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something belonging to the present or the near past, rather than to older times.

clue.text: Here we learn about girl on heath, looking back

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: c (circa) means about, as with dates
lass is a northern British and Scottish word for a girl
a moor is open upland heath

explanation.surface: A story told about a girl on a heath, gazing back over her shoulder, like a Brontë heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here we learn about' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'learn' and 'about' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A classroom is the room in a school where pupils are taught, so it is where learning happens.

clue.text: Share some of driver's licence

indicators.note: some of means only a portion, lifted from inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the apostrophe S and the next word

explanation.surface: Someone asks to share part of another person's driving licence.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the join: driver'S LICEnce.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice is a portion, as in a slice of the profits, which is a person's share.

clue.text: Overly trusting in French spa town, kicked back

indicators.note: a thing kicked back is sent the way it came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: Evian-les-Bains, famous for its bottled mineral water

explanation.surface: A gullible tourist relaxes in a French spa resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicked back' looks like relaxing at the spa, but it turns the town's name round.
explanation.definitionFit: A naive person lacks experience and judgement, so they believe others too readily.

clue.text: Uncomfortable when travelling, gives voice to disgusted expression

blocks.note: to air a view is to voice it
ick is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: An uneasy traveller loudly voices their disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncomfortable when travelling' is loose but fair for the queasiness of a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Airsickness is nausea caused by the motion of an aircraft, one kind of discomfort on a journey.

clue.text: Overwhelmed by destiny, outfit in warship

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed and swallowed up by what overcomes it

blocks.note: fate is destiny
a rig is an outfit of clothes, as in rig-out

explanation.surface: A sailor, crushed by fate, sits aboard a naval ship in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overwhelmed by destiny' reads as despair, but it is an instruction to put the second item inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a naval vessel, historically a fast sailing ship and today a medium-sized escort ship.

clue.text: Evades ruses

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, avoids or sidesteps
second meaning: a plural noun, crafty tricks

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, one a verb and one a noun, each meaning the same answer in a different part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means skilfully avoids something, and the noun means cunning tricks or schemes used to deceive.

clue.text: Let aunt off, accepting kiss that's joyous

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or bad, so these letters are spoiled into a new order
to accept is to take something in, so one part is held inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone lets their aunt off a punishment and gets a happy kiss in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let aunt off' reads as forgiving her; 'off' actually jumbles the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Exultant describes someone triumphantly happy, rejoicing greatly, which is being full of joy.
